rows.jp: 「金曜日、か」
rows.en: “Friday.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Friday, then."

rows.jp: 世界が揺り戻されるまで、あと三日ほど。
rows.en: Roughly three days until the world snaps back.

ghs.en: There remain three days to the swingback of the world.
ghs.assessment: 揺り戻される describes the world being reset, rolled back, or snapping back. 'Swingback' is not a natural noun for this event.

rows.jp: 記憶がなくなって全てリセットされて。
rows.en: Until my memories vanish and everything resets.

ghs.en: Memories will be gone, and all will be reset.

rows.jp: ……うそ寒い。
rows.en: ...The thought sends a chill through me.

ghs.en: ...a bit chilling.

rows.jp: それは死ぬことと大差ないのではないかとも思う。
rows.en: Maybe it isn't so different from dying.

ghs.en: That, I think, just may not be significantly different from death.

rows.jp: この一週間は、誌面の記録にしか残されない。
rows.en: This week will survive only on the page.

ghs.en: Of this one week there will be nothing left but a written report.

rows.jp: 俺がそれを思い返すことはない。
rows.en: I will never remember any of it.

ghs.en: I will never be able to think again about any of this.

rows.jp: 決して。
rows.en: Never.

ghs.en: Never.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 昔。
rows.en: Long ago.

ghs.en: Once upon a time,

rows.jp: こんなゲームで遊んだ。
rows.en: I played a game like this.

ghs.en: there was this videogame I played.

rows.jp: ロープレ。
rows.en: An RPG.

ghs.en: Role playing.

rows.jp: 舞台は未来。
rows.en: Set in the future.

ghs.en: Setting is futuristic.
ghs.assessment: The count noun requires an article or possessive: 'The setting is futuristic' or 'Its setting is the future.'

rows.jp: 世界は荒廃し、人々はドーム都市で生きている。
rows.en: The world lay in ruins, and humanity lived in domed cities.

ghs.en:
The outside world devastated, people live
in domed cities.

rows.jp: 野生動物はモンスター化し、人を襲う。
rows.en: Wild animals had mutated into monsters that preyed on people.

ghs.en:
Wild animals have turned into monsters and
attack the people.

rows.jp: 主人公はモンスターハンター。
rows.en: The hero was a monster hunter.

ghs.en: The protagonist is a monster hunter.

rows.jp: 日常的なクエストから、やがては世界を支配する存在との戦いへ。
rows.en: What began as routine quests eventually became a battle against the entity ruling the world.

ghs.en:
It starts with ordinary quests, then eventually
ends in a fight with the being that rules the
world.

rows.jp: ロープレでは普通、キャラクターが戦闘で敗北すると、魔法や科学等で蘇生させられる。
rows.en: In most RPGs, characters defeated in battle can be revived by magic, science, or what have you.

ghs.en:
In typical RPGs, when characters are defeated in
battle, they can be revived with some magic or
some technological gadget.

rows.jp: 主人公は何度死のうが主人公であり、パーティーが全滅してゲームオーバーにならない限り、危機的な破滅は起こらない。
rows.en: However many times the hero dies, he remains the hero. Unless the entire party is wiped out and it's game over, nothing truly catastrophic happens.

ghs.en:
The protagonist can die as many times as he wants,
but he's the main character; within the limit of
the party not being entirely eliminated, causing
a game over, no complete failure will occur.
ghs.assessment: The protagonist remains the protagonist however many times he dies; the source does not grant him a desire or choice to die. The rest of the sentence has a malformed 'within the limit of' condition and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text: The protagonist can die as many times as he wants

rows.jp: 当然、主観記憶は保持される。
rows.en: Naturally, his first-person memories remain intact.

ghs.en: Naturally, subjective memories would be preserved.

rows.jp: ところがコイツは違った。
rows.en: But this game was different.

ghs.en: Turns out, this one was different.

rows.jp: 主人公のみならず、キャラクターが死ぬと、それは厳然たる死なのである。
rows.en: When any character died—not only the hero—that death was absolute.

ghs.en:
Not just when the main character dies, but if
any character dies, that death is the final kind.
ghs.assessment: 厳然たる死 means an uncompromisingly real or irrevocable death. 'The final kind' is vague and does not state what distinguishes it; intrusive engine line breaks remain.

highlights.text: that death is the final kind

rows.jp: 他の仲間は都市まで戻り、死亡者のクローンをセーブポイントも兼ねる施設に要請する。
rows.en: The surviving party returned to the city and asked a facility that doubled as a save point to make a clone of the dead.

ghs.en:
The other members have to make it back to the
city, and request a clone of the deceased from
the facility that also serves as save point.

rows.jp: 直前のセーブデータ時の主人公が、そこではポンと精製される。
rows.en: Pop: out came the hero exactly as he had been at the last save.

ghs.en:
And pop, the protagonist was restored to just
before the data was saved.
ghs.assessment: The facility produces the protagonist as he existed at the most recent save data. The English places the restored state immediately before that save, shifting the checkpoint backward.

highlights.text:
And pop, the protagonist was restored to just
before the data was saved.

rows.jp: そして誰も何も疑問に思うことなく、冒険は続くのだ。
rows.en: And with no one questioning a thing, the adventure continued.

ghs.en:
And then, without even thinking to question
anything or anyone, the adventure continues.

rows.jp: ショックだった。
rows.en: It shook me.

ghs.en: I was shocked.

rows.jp: セーブ以降の、死んだ主人公の固有時間は、まったく省みられない。
rows.en: No one gave a thought to the dead hero’s unique time since the save.

ghs.en:
The protagonist's eigentime after the save and
before death was never ever re-examinable.
ghs.assessment: The dead protagonist's own elapsed experience after the save is not considered or honored at all. 'Re-examinable' means capable of later inspection and changes disregard into technical impossibility; intrusive line breaks remain.

rows.jp: 同じ主人公なのに、違う人間なんだと思って、プレイした。
rows.en: I played on thinking: he may be the same hero, but he is a different person.

ghs.en:
I thought while playing that while he was the
same protagonist, he was yet a different human.

rows.jp: ゲームは難易度ばかりが高い、バランスの取れていないもので。
rows.en: The game itself had nothing going for it but punishing difficulty and lousy balance.

ghs.en:
The game had nothing to it but a high level of
difficulty, and there was simply no balance.

rows.jp: けど鮮烈な死のイメージがつきまとい、俺は憑かれたように遊び続けた。
rows.en: But its vivid image of death followed me everywhere, and I kept playing as though possessed.

ghs.en:
But I kept playing as if possessed, chasing
after that striking image of death.
ghs.assessment: The vivid image of death haunts or follows him, while he continues playing as if possessed. The English instead makes him voluntarily pursue that image and preserves intrusive engine line breaks.

highlights.text:
But I kept playing as if possessed, chasing
after that striking image of death.

rows.jp: 結末は特攻オチだった。
rows.en: And it all ended with a suicide charge.

ghs.en: Final punchline was a Bolivian Army Ending.

rows.jp: 「……げんなりだ」
rows.en: “...What a downer.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...so dejecting."
ghs.assessment: げんなり describes being weary, disgusted, or thoroughly put off. 'Dejecting' is an unnatural participial adjective for his state.

rows.jp: 自分がそれを体験するとは思わなかった。
rows.en: I never imagined I would experience it myself.

ghs.en: I didn't think I would experience that myself.

rows.jp: してみると俺は何人目なのだろうか。
rows.en: So which version of me am I?

ghs.en: If that's how it is then, I am which number of myself now?
ghs.assessment: He wonders which iteration or number he is. The interrogative phrase cannot serve as the predicate after 'I am' in this word order.

highlights.text: I am which number of myself now?

rows.jp: 五人目。
rows.en: The fifth.

ghs.en: Number five.

rows.jp: 果たして本当にそうなのか。
rows.en: But am I really?

ghs.en: Is that truly what I am, really?

rows.jp: 記録になければ、それを知る手だてはないのだ。
rows.en: Without a record, there is no way to know.

ghs.en: If there are no records, then there is no way to know that.
